residual_risks: checkProvidersDefined now computes bitbucketAPITokenComplete once before the map range, where the original set it lazily during randomized map iteration. The old OAuth count depended on whether the API-token entry had been visited first; the new count is deterministic (1 when both are complete). Callers only compare count to 0, so this is not observable, but the PR's 'behaviour unchanged' claim is slightly loose here. No test pins either behaviour.
testing_gaps: Offline coverage of the refactored production code is minimal. Of the 40 tests in ./internal, 24 pass and 15 skip (live-credential tests). The only offline tests that reach the touched logic are TestCheckProvidersFailureWhenNoneDefined (the 'no providers defined' branch of checkProvidersDefined) and TestFailureIfGitBackupDirUndefined (the first error return of Run/validateStartupConfig). No test references checkProvider, checkJustTokenProvider, checkUserAndPasswordProvider, bitbucketAPITokenDefined, bitbucketOAuthDefined, collectProviderBackupResults, displayXStartupConfig, backupStatusTitle, scheduleBackups, runScheduledJob, createWorkingDir or logRequestTimeout. The partial-config error messages ('%s parameter '%s' is not defined.'), the 0/1 return of checkUserAndPasswordProvider, the Bitbucket API-token-vs-OAuth precedence and the three notify titles could regress without any offline test failing. The gap pre-dates this PR (the original inline code was equally untested), but the PR restructures exactly this logic and claims behaviour is unchanged. Cheap offline guards would be a table test of checkProvider/checkProvidersDefined using t.Setenv (partial Azure/Bitbucket config, blank GitHub token) and a three-case table test of backupStatusTitle.
